subject: Production: Sparrow Health - AZ1 network split and failover coordination
messages:
From: Liam Wong <liam.wong@sparrowhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@sparrowhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Production: high 5xx and tail latency in us-east-1

Diego / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and a 4–7x spike in tail latency for our production traffic hitting us-east-1 (AZ1) starting ~08:45 ET. Error rate is ~18% for the last 20 minutes and throughput is degraded — some of our flows are timing out and retrying. This is impacting checkout flows for Sparrow Portal users.

Attached: sparrow-logs-tail-1019.txt (truncated logs)

Can you please start an incident bridge and advise next steps? We need ETA on mitigation and whether you'll route traffic cross-region.

—Liam
Liam Wong
Sparrow Health — Head of Platform
liam.wong@sparrowhealth.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Liam Wong <liam.wong@sparrowhealth.com>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@sparrowhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production: high 5xx and tail latency in us-east-1

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're standing up an incident bridge now (Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/876-bridge) and pulling telemetry.

What we see so far: KV cache evictions in AZ1 causing cache-miss amplification; several inference workers returning 502/503 due to a networking partition between AZ1 and the regional NLB. Plan: 1) open bridge, 2) initiate routing override to shift a percentage of traffic to us-west-2, 3) enable quantized fallback model in us-west-2 to preserve throughput while we stabilize.

I'm on the bridge. We'll keep you updated and aim for an initial mitigation step in the next 15 minutes.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: c-suite-ops@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Production: high 5xx and tail latency in us-east-1 — mitigation proposal

Forwarding Diego's note and adding context for ops/execs.

Summary of recommended actions from infra/serving:
- Immediate routing override: shift 35% of affected customer routes from us-east-1 to us-west-2.
- Enable quantized model variant in us-west-2 as a fallback; the variant has slightly higher latency but lower GPU memory pressure.
- Temporarily relax model-pin constraints for Sparrow's routes for 30 minutes to allow variant fallback.

Risks & asks: relaxing model pins may change tokens/costs and could slightly alter inference outputs (fallback variant is verified for Sparrow via evaluation run earlier this year). We should authorize up to a 15% credit for impacted tokens as a customer goodwill gesture, and approve a one-time capacity burst on Dedicated for 30 minutes if we need extra throughput in us-west-2.

Requesting quick decision from C-suite ops: approve credit and burst capacity to complete mitigation. Diego — please keep the customer updated on expected timeline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: infra-oncall@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: ACTION: route override + routing policy change (Sparrow)

Infra — please apply the following temporary override for Sparrow Health (SPW-2026-014):
- Route match: customer_id=SPW-2026-014 AND region=us-east-1
- Action: split 35% -> us-west-2, 65% -> us-east-1 (sticky by session)
- Allow fallback model variant: sparrow-gpt-large-quant (TTL 30m)

Attached: route-override-stub.json

I've notified billing/finance for the potential credit. Diego — confirm once routing changes are live so I can update Sparrow's ops contact.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Product Manager, Routing | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 10:01:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ACTION: route override + routing policy change (Sparrow)

Update from infra: routing override applied at 09:42 ET. Observed results: 5xx error rate for Sparrow traffic dropped from 18% -> 4% within 7 minutes. Tail latency for routed requests to us-west-2 is higher (~1.6x) but throughput stabilized. We are seeing KV cache warm-up in the new region; some prefix cache misses logged (attached kv-cache-evictions.csv).

As suspected, to keep latency from increasing further we need a short Dedicated capacity burst in us-west-2 (estimated +2 GPUs for 30 minutes). Marissa, exec approval required for burst and credit. If approved, infra can enable burst in ~6 minutes.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Liam Wong <liam.wong@sparrowhealth.com>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@sparrowhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 12:02:00 -0400
Subject: RESOLVED: Sparrow Health - partial mitigation and next steps

Liam / Emily —

Summary: we observed a network partition between AZ1 and the regional NLB causing cache evictions and worker 502/503s. Mitigation steps completed:
- Temporary routing override applied (35% -> us-west-2) at 09:42 ET; 5xx reduced to ~4% within 7 minutes.
- Quantized fallback model enabled in us-west-2 to preserve throughput while we warm caches.
- Requested Dedicated capacity burst approved and applied at 09:50 ET (2 GPUs for 30 mins) — this lowered tail latency further.

Impact: short-lived increase in tail latency for the routed traffic while caches warmed; some requests saw slightly different responses due to the quantized variant. Overall customer-facing error rate and throughput returned to acceptable thresholds by ~10:05 ET.

Next steps:
- Postmortem doc (will share link) and targeted fix to prevent cross-AZ NLB partitions recurring.
- We'll provide a one-time credit equal to 15% of impacted token spend as a commercial remedy; billing team will follow up.
- Schedule a technical review with Sparrow engineering to validate fallback variants and expand readiness playbooks.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the full postmortem within 72 hours. If you'd like a bridge recap call, I'm available this afternoon.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
Diego_fernandez@redwood.com
